headline: VIX near 36 after Friday's AI rout; Nasdaq-100 near bear-market territory per Cboe

what_happened.summary: The Cboe Daily Take 'Market Selloff Deepens as Investors Seek Shelter' (20 Nov) says Friday did not look like dip-buying. The S&P 500 and Dow closed in correction territory, the S&P 500 broke below 7,000, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3%. Cboe says the Nasdaq 100 was dangerously close to a bear market (a 20% or larger decline). Cboe volatility surged: VIX 35.89 (+26.20%), its highest since April 2025 per Cboe, VXN 45.25 and COR1M 36.05. Treasury yields fell sharply as money sought shelter. Unverified headlines this morning describe a futures bounce. The inputs have no live prices, so this brief does not say where NQ trades.
what_happened.market_action: FRED's Nasdaq-100 close only runs to 19 Nov (26517.05, -2.21%), so Friday's index close is not in the numbers. Cboe says the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the Nasdaq 100 was close to bear-market territory. Cboe volatility on 20 Nov: VIX 35.89 (+26.20%), VXN 45.25 (+24.04%), VVIX 138.03 (+8.60%), VIX9D 40.72 (+39.17%), COR1M 36.05 (+19.29%), SKEW 138.84 (-1.43%). Engine read: the near-term VIX9D, VIX and VVIX jump together with COR1M climbing from 11.8 on 13 Nov to 36.05 means the market is pricing a broad, correlated drawdown, not just a tech rotation. SKEW easing while VIX spikes fits a spot-driven vol rise.
what_happened.macro: US Treasury: 2-year 4.63% (-13.0 bp), 10-year 4.92% (-12.0 bp), 30-year 5.31% (-9.0 bp) on 20 Nov. FRED shows the 10-year breakeven at 2.15% and the 10-year real yield at 2.88% (19 Nov). Polymarket has a 25 bps December hike at 92.5%, 50+ bps at 2.4% and no change at 4.9% (prediction-market prices, not CME FedWatch). Latest BLS prints: October CPI +0.35% m/m, core CPI +0.3%, unemployment 4.1%, payrolls +165.0k. FRED shows September core PCE at 3.12% y/y. HY OAS was 3.52 on 19 Nov (+5.0 bp), wider on every observation since 13 Nov. Engine read: yields fell with equities, so this looks like a flight to safety, not a rates-driven selloff.
what_happened.geopolitics: Cboe says conflicts in the Middle East are unresolved and mentions US-Iran tensions. FRED oil data is stale to 17 Nov (Brent 92.94, WTI 89.53). Headlines this morning mix supply-surplus worries with renewed Middle East shipping attacks; both are unverified.
what_happened.company_news: Cboe says Nvidia fell nearly 14% on reports that the SEC is investigating its accounting practices, and that it has lost $1.4 trillion of market cap since the 8 Nov Huang scandal. Cboe says Anthropic lost more than 9% on Friday after its Thursday debut. The Cboe 'Anthropic Options Preview' says ANT options start trading today, Mon 23 Nov. A headline from Barron's says Trump urged Nvidia's board to rehire Huang; this is unverified. A headline also says CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler (unverified).

driver_reason: Cboe ties Friday's leg lower to the Nvidia SEC-probe reports, the Anthropic post-IPO slide and the wider AI selloff. Volatility and positioning are amplifying it (VIX 35.89, VIX9D 40.72, COR1M 36.05), but the trigger was still AI and chip-sector news; rates eased.
leader_reason: Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 was -0.19 pct pts on 19 Nov and -0.78 over 5 sessions, and VXN minus VIX is 9.36 pts, so Nasdaq-100 vol still carries a premium. COR1M at 36.05 shows the selling is broadening, but Cboe still places tech and semiconductors at the centre, and the Nasdaq Composite's 5.3% drop on Friday was far larger than the S&P 500 move Cboe describes.

The 'oversold bounce' narrative in this morning's headlines is repeated across many outlets without independent evidence and is not a signal on its own.

memory_update.running_thesis: Friday 20 Nov (Cboe) was the deepest leg yet: S&P 500 and Dow in correction, the Nasdaq Composite down 5.3%, and the Nasdaq 100 near bear territory. Nvidia fell nearly 14% on SEC accounting-probe reports and Anthropic fell more than 9%. VIX 35.89, VXN 45.25, COR1M 36.05, VVIX 138.03: contagion is broad. Yields fell sharply (10-year 4.92%) as a flight to safety, while a 9 Dec hike is priced (Polymarket 25 bps 92.5%). HY OAS 3.52 as of 19 Nov. Unverified headlines point to a Monday bounce. ANT options start 23 Nov. Oil data stale to 17 Nov.
open_questions: Does a Monday bounce hold, or is this a bear-market leg?
Does the Nvidia SEC probe spread to other chipmakers (AMD allegations are open)?
Do credit spreads keep widening after four straight wider prints to 19 Nov?
Do 50+ bps hike odds rise again before 9 Dec, or does the equity damage soften the Fed?
